headline: Indonesia Reports State Budget Deficit Of Rp379 Trillion For October
seoTitle: Indonesia Reports October 2026 State Budget Performance
metaDescription: The Indonesian government announced a state budget deficit of Rp379.3 trillion as of October 2026, maintaining a 1.47 percent GDP ratio.
aiSummaryBullets: The Indonesian government recorded a state budget deficit of Rp379.3 trillion by October 2026, representing 1.47 percent of the national GDP.
Customs and excise revenue reached Rp267.2 trillion for the year up to October, while total government spending hit Rp2,997 trillion.
Financial authorities clarified that the budget deficit does not constitute a state loss, stating the current fiscal performance remains on track.
aiContextParagraph: Government officials have provided an update on Indonesia's state budget (APBN) performance as of October 2026, highlighting a deficit of Rp379.3 trillion, or 1.47 percent of the gross domestic product. Finance Ministry representatives emphasized that this deficit should not be interpreted as a financial loss for the country, describing the current fiscal situation as being on track. Supporting data points reveal that customs and excise receipts reached Rp267.2 trillion for the period, while total government expenditures amounted to Rp2,997 trillion. Alongside these macroeconomic figures, separate industry updates noted that Antam reported significant growth in nickel sales and ore production through September 2026. Additionally, Pertamina recorded an average oil and gas production rate of 935,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day during the first half of the year.
whyItIsViral: The story has gained significant attention across major Indonesian news outlets due to the release of key national fiscal performance metrics.
